---
title: "Session 13 guided lab · Repeat checked operations"
---

Work in **BIOS6301-mywork.Rproj**. Copy the starter from the separate
BIOS6301-materials clone into `work/session13/` in your personal repository.
Choose [Quarto](starter/iteration-lab.qmd) or [R Markdown](starter/iteration-lab.Rmd).
Render or Knit your copy. All supplied inputs are synthetic.

## 1. Start with a checked operation

The starter supplies the Session 11 helpers, following the contract protected in
Session 12, and the same marker table. Run the supplied checks before iterating.
`one_summary(x)` must return a numeric vector named `n`, `mean`, and `sd`.
Use observed n; return numeric `NA` for the mean with no observations and for
SD with fewer than two observations. Reject invalid input through `safe_mean()`.

## 2. Loops and allocation

Build a matrix with three rows and one column per marker. Preallocate it with
row names `n`, `mean`, `sd` and marker column names. Fill it using
`seq_along(markers)` and `markers[[j]]`. Preserve a 3-by-0 matrix for zero columns.
First practice the simpler scalar case with one `safe_mean()` result per column.

## 3. Vectorized operations

For the supplied numeric matrix, compute one row mean using each of a
preallocated loop, `apply(..., 1, mean)`, and `rowMeans()`.
Use the same missing-value rule in all three. Verify numerical equivalence before
measuring. Add a character ID column to a copy, inspect `as.matrix()`, and explain
why the mixed data frame is not a safe input for numeric matrix summaries.

## 4. Lists and typed outputs

1. Apply `one_summary()` with `lapply()` and `vapply()` using
   `c(n = 0, mean = 0, sd = 0)` as the template. Compare against the loop's
   values, names, types, and dimensions.
2. Check ordinary, all-missing, one-observation, and zero-column cases.
3. Replace a marker with a character vector. Show that the helper rejects it.
   Explain why an output template alone cannot detect every invalid input.
4. Use a named list of unequal-length numeric vectors with `lapply()` and
   `vapply(..., safe_mean, numeric(1))`. Different input lengths do not imply
   different output lengths when the operation returns one mean.

## 5. Base R and optional purrr

Use `Map(change_summary, baseline_columns, followup_columns)` for the two supplied
paired lists. Check list lengths and matching names before mapping, then compare
with a preallocated list filled by a loop. Each helper checks its paired vectors.

Optional equivalents: `map(markers, one_summary)` returns a list;
`map_dbl(markers, safe_mean)` returns one number per marker. `map_dbl()` cannot
hold all three statistics from `one_summary()` in one element. For paired
lists, compare `map2()` with `Map()`.

## 6. Choose and combine results

Create one data-frame row per marker, including the marker name and three
statistics. Collect the rows in a preallocated list and bind once. State the
zero-column output schema explicitly. Explain when an ordinary loop is clearer
than an independent mapping, especially when the next step uses the previous state.

## 7. Verify and measure

Compare the supplied growing and preallocated square-root loops on the same
input, checking equality first. Warm up both implementations and record at least
five repetitions with `system.time()`. Do the same for the row-summary implementations.
Report input dimensions, R version, repetition count, and observed variation.
A zero elapsed time can be below timer resolution; do not claim infinite speedup.

Record `object.size()` for the input and final outputs. Explain that these are
stored object-size estimates, not peak memory measurements. Recommend a solution
using correctness, output shape, readability, and your actual measurements.

## Exit evidence

Submit the checked helpers, iteration results, empty/invalid cases, equivalence
checks, timing context, and recommendation. No hypothesis tests, confidence
intervals, or simulation study design are required in this programming lab.

## Optional bounded-loop practice

Starting at `x = 1`, repeatedly divide by two until `x < 0.01`, with an explicit
maximum iteration count. Record whether the threshold or iteration limit ended
the loop. Explain why the next input depends on the previous output.
